text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) said on Monday it has signed a memorandum of agreement to buy a 60 percent stake in PNB-Republic Bank at a cost of 880 million pesos.
Maybank said in a statement that it has received a notice of award by the Philippine National Bank (PNB) for the acquisition.
PNB in October last year announced the terms of offer for the sale of the bank, for which Maybank had submitted a conditional bid on December 23.
Maybank, Malaysia's largest banking group, was the only bidder for the 60 percent stake. PNB will retain its 40 percent stake in the Filipino bank.
The management of PNB-Republic will be handed over to Maybank.
PNB-Republic has a network of 60 domestic branches, 24 of which are in the Metro Manila area.
Analysts have said that the Philippine acquisition is another move in Maybank's strategy to become a regional banking group.
In a speech at the signing ceremony in Manila, Maybank chairman Mohamed Basir Ahmad said the acquisition extended its international network to 13 countries.
"This extension is part of Maybank's objectives to meet the needs of our customers, particularly Malaysian customers who are increasingly establishing trade ties and investing abroad," Basir said.
